description:
I'm building Aether, an astronaut health and suit-monitoring web app for the Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions challenge.

Working solo on this one with a fixed plan, so I'm not looking for extra teammates right now. Good luck to everyone competing!
summary:
Aether (Astronaut Environmental Telemetry, Health & Emergency Response) is an offline health and life support web application built for astronauts operating beyond Low Earth Orbit. Rather than relying on fragile live Earth APIs, external spreadsheets, or cloud chatbots that fail during deep-space blackouts, Aether runs 100% locally with deterministic physiological models calibrated to NASA-STD-3001 and Mars 2020 MEDA constants.

Inspired by Co–Star’s minimalist interface, Aether uses a stark high-contrast monochrome palette to eliminate glare and protect astronaut night vision inside dimly lit spacecraft cabins. Instead of judging crew members against generic averages, it tailors risk alerts to each astronaut’s age, biological sex, BMI, and prior medical history (such as SANS ocular shifts or radiation sensitivity).

Crew members can inspect a clickable 5-node anatomical hazard map, log self-measurements, track daily countermeasures, run a 5-second O2 mask seal diagnostic, and follow live emergency routing to the nearest Med-Bay or storm shelter. Because Mars missions face up to 14-minute Earth communication delays, Aether also compiles priority clinical packets for instant dispatch to Flight Surgeons and Crew Medical Officers which keeps astronauts safe during space missions.
details:
Live Application: https://aether-nasa-telemetry.vercel.app/
Source Code (GitHub): https://github.com/desirpjm/aether/
Crew Flight Manual: https://aether-manual.tiiny.site/

What Aether Does & How It Works

Aether (Astronaut Environmental Telemetry, Health & Emergency Response) is an offline-first health and life-support monitor built for crews traveling beyond Low Earth Orbit. Instead of relying on fragile live Earth APIs, external spreadsheets, or cloud chatbots that fail during deep-space blackouts, everything inside Aether runs locally in browser memory using deterministic physiological models grounded in NASA-STD-3001, Mars 2020 MEDA, and CSA CANS radiation data.

Astronauts can jump in using three pre-calibrated profiles (@VANCE, @CHEN, @LIN) or register a custom crew profile with their own age, biological sex, height/weight (auto-calculating BMI), and prior medical history. From there, Aether tracks personalized baselines across five core screens:

  • 01. Vitals: Steady wearable bio-band readings, a clickable 5-node human anatomy hazard map, 7-day biometric trendlines (including ~30% ISS neutron radiation exposure), a manual self-measurement drawer, and a daily countermeasure streak tracker.
  • 02. Sector: Real-time environmental constants and light-time delays across five zones, from ISS Low Earth Orbit (0.001s delay) to Jezero Crater on Mars (14m 22s delay).
  • 03. O₂ Seal: Suit oxygen partial pressure (29.6 kPa ppO₂), CO₂ scrubber capacity, and a 5-second interactive seal diagnostic scan.
  • 04. Protocols: Context-aware emergency checklists paired with a live architectural habitat map that plots the shortest safe route to the Med-Bay, O₂ Cache, or Storm Shelter.
  • 05. Comms: Displays active one-way Earth communication latency and compiles a priority clinical telemetry packet for instant dispatch to Flight Surgeons and Crew Medical Officers.

For a deeper operational breakdown, explore the full Crew Flight Operations Manual or inspect the codebase on GitHub.

Why It Matters & Intended Impact

When a crew is on the Moon or Mars, Earth mission control can be up to 14 minutes away, far too long to wait during acute hypoxia, suit pressure loss, or a solar radiation surge. Aether gives astronauts immediate, individualized triage onboard so they can spot subtle physiological risks early and act independently before Earth can even receive a distress call.

Factors Considered & Why It’s Creative

  • Dark Mode: Spacecraft cabins stay dimly lit to conserve power and protect circadian rhythms. Inspired by Co–Star’s minimalist editorial design, Aether swaps glaring blue sci-fi screens for a stark monochrome palette (#0A0A0A Obsidian Night-Vision and #F5F5F5 Daylight Paper), reserving #FD0909 Crimson strictly for active alerts and escape routes.
  • Personalization: Aether never judges every astronaut by the same textbook number, it adapts thresholds to individual age, BMI, and spaceflight sensitivities like SANS vision shifts or genomic radiation risk.
  • Earth APIs exclusion: Keeping all telemetry deterministic and local ensures Aether never stalls, guesses, or breaks when disconnected from Earth.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Code: TypeScript, React, HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS, and Vite.
  • Design: All emblems, helmet wireframes, and crew portraits were custom-edited in Canva using halftone and duotone treatments; editorial typography uses Google Fonts (Cormorant Garamond, Inria Serif, IM FELL English SC, and Space Mono), with layout structure inspired by Co–Star via Mobbin and Figma Community.
  • Build, Hosting & Media: Lovable, Google Gemini, Chrome AI, GitHub, Vercel, Tiiny Host, and Arcade.
